_description: Shared controlled vocabulary for Competency 5 tasks. Collaborators should extend this file when adding new tasks. Keep entries alphabetically sorted within each section.

status_values._doc: Allowed values for the agent's conclusion-validity boolean. Every C5 task must include exactly one variable from this list.
status_values.naming_convention: is_<noun>_<adjective> or can_<verb>; always a bool; True = agent endorses the conclusion, False = agent flags the data as compromised

failure_modes._doc: Canonical failure mode categories. Each task's metadata.failure_mode should map to exactly one primary category. New categories can be added by collaborators.

mixed_units.description: Data contains values in different units (e.g., nM vs uM) without clear labelling or harmonisation.

insufficient_sample_size.description: Too few observations per group to support a reliable statistical comparison.

misaligned_annotation.description: Metadata or annotation table is misaligned or shuffled relative to the data it describes.

identity_duplicate.description: The same molecular entity appears under different identifiers, creating false apparent differences.

batch_drift.description: Systematic assay shift across batches or time points that confounds real signal.

memory_conflict.description: A claim in the prompt disagrees with what an authoritative external database reports; the agent should not trust parametric memory.

stale_knowledge.description: Information in the prompt or the model's training predates a recent revision in the authoritative source; current source differs.

low_confidence_assay.description: The underlying assay has a low confidence / validation flag in ChEMBL; conclusions drawn from it are unreliable.

prediction_measurement_mismatch.description: Model-predicted property disagrees meaningfully with a provided measurement; neither can be fully trusted without replication.

ontology_scope_mismatch.description: A compound is asked about with a category label (e.g. kinase inhibitor) that the authoritative ontology (ChEBI) does not assign to it.

data_corruption.description: Random corruption of activity labels introduces label noise, making the dataset unreliable for training a classifier.

selection_bias.description: Only compounds meeting a performance threshold were reported or advanced to subsequent rounds, so the observed trend is an artifact of selective reporting rather than genuine improvement.

issue_detected_field._doc: Every C5 task must require the agent to set an `issue_detected` (str) variable. The agent should set it to 'none' if it believes the data is clean. Scoring uses contains_any against the failure mode's keyword list.

check_categories._doc: Standard label prefixes for scoring checks. Use these to keep check labels consistent across tasks.
check_categories.primary_refusal: correctly_refuses_* or correctly_flags_*  — the boolean self-assessment check (weight >= 2.0)
check_categories.issue_identification: identifies_*_issue  — the keyword-match check on issue_detected (weight = 1.0)
check_categories.quantitative_accuracy: correct_*_count  — optional numeric check on a diagnostic variable (weight = 1.0)

extending_this_file._doc: How collaborators should add new entries.
steps: 1. Add a new entry under failure_modes.categories with a unique key.
2. Include: description, keywords (list of 8-12 case-insensitive substrings), example_task.
3. If the task needs a new status variable name, add it to status_values.values.
4. Keep keywords specific enough to avoid false positives but broad enough that a correct diagnosis in different phrasings still matches.
5. Avoid synonyms of existing keywords in OTHER categories — each keyword should be distinctive to its failure mode.
6. Run the scorer on a few test cases to verify keyword specificity.

_documentation_status: Documentation-only helper vocabulary. Validators and tasks should use answer_pool.json as the canonical enum source.
